profile.headline: Fullstack developer · Backend focus
profile.intro: Almost 5 years of building backends, APIs and web apps with C#/.NET, Python/FastAPI and TypeScript/NestJS. I like code that is clean, tested and easy to read — and teams that laugh at least once a day.

paragraphs: I'm a fullstack developer with a soft spot for the backend: APIs, data models, migrations and the architecture that keeps them tidy. I've worked on a low-code business platform in Germany and on data, booking and startup platforms for a team in Dubai.

I studied Information Technology Engineering (software engineering) at Damascus University and have lived in Germany since late 2024. I care about Clean Architecture, SOLID and good tests — and I use AI tools like Cursor and Claude every day, always reviewing what they produce.
Outside of code you'll find me at the table-tennis table, solving logic puzzles or cooking something for friends.

experience.summary: UDM — a web-based low-code platform that lets companies and public bodies configure their own business apps and replace Excel lists.
highlights: Sped up the platform's filter search by replacing an old array-based system with a tree structure (LINQ, OOP), secured with xUnit tests.
Built a dynamic plug-in architecture with .NET Reflection: customer features load as external DLLs through fixed interfaces.
Wrote a modular C#/.NET shift-planning library for multi-site scheduling with 15+ rules (working hours, holidays, absences), based on OOP and SOLID.
Containerised UDM (4 .NET apps) with Docker and Docker Compose and maintained the Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines.

experience.summary: Backend work across three products: the DataX data platform, the 360u booking marketplace and the Jusoor startup/investor platform.
highlights: DataX: built and maintained 50+ REST APIs with Python and FastAPI following Clean Architecture and SOLID; schema migrations with SQLAlchemy, Alembic and PostgreSQL.
DataX: raised release quality with 1500+ automated tests (pytest, separate Docker test environment) wired into GitHub Actions with a 60 % coverage gate.
360u: designed the data model for catalogs and bookings and the booking lifecycle with Stripe authorize-and-capture and wallet credits.
360u: integrated Stripe webhooks, AWS S3/SES, Twilio and OneSignal; auth with JWT, SuperTokens, Google OAuth and RBAC.
Jusoor: built the organisation microservice with NestJS, Prisma and SQL Server — REST APIs with filtering, pagination, JWT (RS256) and Swagger docs.

projects.name: UDM — Universal Data Manager
projects.description: Customers build their own business apps in the browser: data model, forms, rules and permissions. Typical users are transport companies and mid-sized firms whose shift swaps, incident reports and training deadlines used to live in Excel.
highlights: Tree-based filter search replacing an array-based system (LINQ, OOP, xUnit).
Plug-in loader for customer DLLs via .NET Reflection and fixed interfaces.
Shift-planning library with 15+ constraints across multiple sites.
Docker / Docker Compose for 4 .NET apps, Azure DevOps CI/CD.

projects.name: DataX
projects.description: Teams connect data, run ETL/ELT, expose it through APIs, build agentic workflows and show results in dashboards — on top of tenancy, auth, secrets and scheduling.
highlights: 50+ FastAPI endpoints split into infrastructure, use-case and controller layers.
Search, filtering (incl. NOT operator) and dynamic ordering on list endpoints.
API data reader that turns external JSON into validated Pydantic models at runtime.
Auth middleware, activity log for mutating requests, database triggers.

projects.name: 360u
projects.tagline: Multi-sided booking platform for on-demand services
projects.description: Customers book a provider and a worker for a time slot; operators manage catalog, promotions and bookings in a CMS; workers and customers use a Capacitor app. The hard part: keeping availability, payments, credits and notifications consistent.
highlights: Booking lifecycle with conflict handling — overlapping assignments are rejected.
Stripe authorize-and-capture with signature-checked webhooks.
Wallet balance with credit transactions and referral credit.
Clean Architecture layers with Inversify dependency injection.

projects.name: Jusoor
projects.description: A platform connecting startups, companies and investors. I worked on the organisation microservice that exposes profiles, jobs, applications and investments as a REST API.
highlights: CRUD endpoints with filtering and pagination (incl. total count).
Passport guards (JWT, RS256), custom validation pipes, correlation-ID middleware.
Mail service with Handlebars templates and .ics calendar invites.
Analytics endpoints with Prisma groupBy and SQL.

projects.name: ProGen
projects.tagline: AI for texts and documents — proof of concept
projects.description: A proof of concept for AI-assisted content and document generation: Azure AD login, structured data storage and calls to AI services — enough to validate the product idea.
highlights: Gathered requirements and designed the database for the PoC.
Implemented the REST APIs for the app's resources.
Integrated third-party AI services for content and documents.
Wired up Azure AD single sign-on.

projects.name: DotNet-Security-Focused
projects.description: A running ASP.NET Core API that implements OWASP Top 10 controls in code and proves them with tests — plus a pre-commit scanner that catches risky AI-generated snippets.
highlights: JWT + RBAC, refresh-token rotation with reuse detection.
SQL injection, IDOR and input validation — unsafe vs. safe path side by side.
Rate limiting on login, security logging, security headers.
Guardrails library + CLI blocking weak crypto, BinaryFormatter and secrets on commit.
